report: Checked all 13 candidate lemmas; every difference is licensed by the ASV's English or the construction, and no construction is analysed two ways across verses.

The repeated formula אֵין עֹשֵׂה־טוֹב (vv. 1, 3) is aligned identically both times: אֵין → There is none headed on none (rule 50), the anarthrous participle → that doeth (rule 46), טוֹב → good. The two כִּי of v. 5 take the different connectives the ASV wrote (For / because). The two הֲ differ because v. 2 embeds an indirect question (if, rule 17) while v. 4 marks the question by fronting the light verb Have, which is יָדְעוּ's own rendering, so the particle is unrepresented (rule 17 inversion-alone, rule 43's fronted possessive verb by analogy).

Read the dump for added units: as (v. 4), And (v. 4), where (v. 5), them (v. 5), were come (v. 6), Then (v. 6), and (v. 6) all answer to no morpheme, and nothing elsewhere in the chapter folds a comparable word into a neighbour, so there is no hidden split.

BSB disagreements: גַּם (v. 3) and הֲ (v. 4) are convention differences, not errors. The ASV's no, not one spends its not on the negation, which אֵין already carries, and גַּם's additive sense is unwritten; the v. 4 Have is the lexical light verb of have knowledge rather than a question auxiliary. Both units name the competing reading.

Hedged single-occurrence judgments left standing as noted: great in in great fear (v. 5) read as the cognate accusative's intensification; up in eat up (v. 4) read as part of the devour rendering; were come (v. 6) left added beside the fixed optative Oh that; set to (v. 0) headed on set under rule 24's fixed-phrase sentence.
The two repeated notes the report flags (Rule 19; supplied the on the construct) restate contract rules and need no convention. Nothing here generalises; no promotions or amendments.
